facts.F48: Keep rule has one owner: OrphanedFeatureCleanupService.CleanupAsync, a domain-service policy over the whole Feature set (it reads other Features, so it is cross-aggregate). A Feature is kept iff it is in a Portfolio or its ReferenceId is the ParentReferenceId of a Feature that is in a Portfolio; every other Feature is deleted set-based with ExecuteDeleteAsync. The two clauses are named private static Expression<Func<Feature,bool>> members (IsInAPortfolio, ParentsAPortfolioFeature) so the rule is written once. Rejected: a query method on IFeatureRepository (a second place deciding the same fact); a method on Feature (the rule reads other rows, not one object's data).
facts.F49: IsParentFeature stops deciding the clean-up. The column and its write in WorkItemService.RefreshParentFeatures stay unchanged (migrations are expand-only: no drop, no rename). Its other reader, WorkItemService.RefreshFeatures (keeps flagged items out of blocked-edge detection), is unchanged and out of scope. The WorkItemService comment above TheSweepDidNotVouchForThisParent that names !f.IsParentFeature as the clean-up rule is reworded in S3. No API DTO or frontend code reads the flag; a child's Parent column resolves its parent by ReferenceId and needs only the stored row. Rejected: dropping the column (expand-only); maintaining the flag on update (no reader needs it any more).

facts.F50: Remaining work of a Feature in no Portfolio is removed by the same clean-up: after the Feature delete, CleanupAsync deletes every FeatureWork row whose Feature is in no Portfolio (ExecuteDeleteAsync). Rows are deleted, not zeroed, because FeatureRepository.FeaturesOfTeam and FeaturesWorkedOnBy select by FeatureWork row existence; Feature.ClearFeatureWork only zeroes counts and would leave the item on the Team tab. WhenForecast and StartForecast rows of a kept parent are left alone (P5); with no FeatureWork it is in no forecast set and on no Team page. Rejected: a 'Feature left its last Portfolio' domain event (covers only future departures, so existing instances would still need the sweep: two owners of one fact); clearing inline in WorkItemService.RefreshRemainingWork (it loops only the Portfolio's current Features and misses Portfolio delete and start).
facts.F51: Portfolio delete runs the clean-up at once through a new domain event PortfolioDeleted(int PortfolioId) in Models/Events, published by PortfolioController.DeletePortfolio's queued lambda after the save, as TeamController publishes TeamDeleted. A new handler PortfolioDeletedOrphanedFeatureCleanupHandler in Modules/WorkItems/Application/Policies calls IOrphanedFeatureCleanupService.CleanupAsync and is registered in Program.cs beside the TeamDeleted handlers. PortfolioRepository.Remove stops deleting Features (RemoveOrphanedFeatures goes): today it is a second owner of the orphan rule and deletes a Feature that still parents a Feature in another Portfolio. Rejected: calling the clean-up directly in the controller lambda (the decision would sit in a driving adapter, and ADR-270 lists Portfolio deleted as a fact with no event); keeping RemoveOrphanedFeatures (duplicate rule that contradicts maintainer decision A1).
facts.F52: Existing instances need no migration: the startup clean-up (Program.RunStartupOrphanedFeatureCleanupAsync) and the clean-up in the finally of every PortfolioUpdater run call the same CleanupAsync, so the new rule applies at the next start or refresh. The refreshed Portfolio's forecast is enqueued by forecastUpdater.TriggerUpdate and runs after that clean-up; its input fingerprint changes because the gathered Feature set changed, so it recomputes and the stranded Feature no longer takes Team throughput.
facts.F53: Churn ends by the keep rule alone: a parent stored unflagged (downloaded by the Feature half) is kept while a Portfolio Feature names it, and RefreshParentFeatures finds the row by ReferenceId and updates it (TheStoredFeatureFor), never re-creating it. Once PortfolioRepository.Remove stops deleting Features, the clean-up is the only production path that deletes Features.
facts.F54: Claim-to-checker: the keep rule, the removal of remaining work outside every Portfolio and no-churn are finite state-safety claims over Features, Portfolio memberships and parent links, checked in Quint (model docs/feature/bug-6665-former-parents-stranded/models/keepRule.qnt): simulation with quint run and a bounded check with quint verify on the Apalache backend. No Agda proof is needed (no totality or arithmetic claim). Liveness does not apply: the clean-up is a synchronous step at the end of every refresh, Portfolio delete and start; nothing promises eventual progress beyond that step running.
facts.F55: Context map: Work Items context only (ADR-270). New domain event PortfolioDeleted, published where the Portfolio is deleted (a controller today, as for TeamDeleted) and handled in Work Items; it closes ADR-270's gap 'facts with no event: Portfolio deleted'. New Work Items glossary term: Orphaned Feature, a Feature in no Portfolio that parents no Feature in a Portfolio; the clean-up deletes it. ADR-270 (gap list, event-to-context list, glossary) and ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 are updated at finalize. No UI surface change.
